9-Q/20/2026

Resolution submitted to ascertain the view of members of the People's Majlis on the government's decision to remove fourteen plots of land of the Malé City Council from the council's jurisdiction and designate them as state property.

Preamble

This is a resolution submitted under Article 189 of the Rules of Procedure of the Majlis to ascertain the view of members of the 20th People's Majlis on this matter, as the decision made by the Ministry of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development, under the Law on the 19th Amendment to Law No. 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act of the Maldives), to remove fourteen (14) plots of land of the Malé City Council from that council's jurisdiction and transfer them to state ownership is considered a decision that narrows the powers of councils and obstructs the decentralised system.

Resolution

Whereas Article 56-2(c) of the Law on the 19th Amendment to Law No. 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act of the Maldives) states that, with regard to land and premises within a council's jurisdiction, the Cabinet may decide to remove a plot of land or premises within the council's jurisdiction in order for the government to carry out development projects,

[stamp: Secretariat of the People's Majlis; 4175; 8:05; Dhumari; 26.10.26; D; 26/10/2026]
[signature]

Whereas Article 56-2(d) of Law No. 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act of the Maldives) states that, before removing a plot of land or premises within a council's jurisdiction from the council's jurisdiction, information about the development project must be shared with the council of the island or city where the project is decided to be carried out, and the council's views and consultation must be sought,

Whereas Article 56-2(d) of Law No. 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act of the Maldives) states that information on the land or premises decided to be removed from the council's jurisdiction, and information on the development project the government designates to carry out on that land or premises, must be made public,

Whereas the Ministry of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development has decided to remove 14 (fourteen) plots of land from the council's jurisdiction and transfer them to state ownership, stating that they are plots essential for urban development work needed for the population of Malé and Villimale', and for providing infrastructure services and further expanding those services, without disclosing any details other than the names of the projects designated to be carried out on those plots, and without any consultation with, or even sharing with, the City Council,

Accordingly, the plots removed from the Malé City Council are:

1. Sultan Park (historic area and museum [?])

[signature]

2. Rasfannu (nothing further to be done)

3. Reclaimed area of the fish market ward (a fish market)

4. Thaisa Kori (temporary [?] by the Malé Infrastructure Development Project)

5. Fish market (an office and commercial building)

6. Fishermen's ground (a pump station)

7. [?] market (a mixed-use commercial building)

8. Carnival (a residential and commercial building)

9. [?] school plot (upgrading and building additional facilities)

10. G Building No. 2 (public restroom and additional facilities)

11. Project site used by Villa Hakatha (an electric vehicle charging facility project)

12. [?] park (a parking building and a mixed-use commercial building)

13. National stadium [?] plot (a conference and exhibition centre and a [?] [?] centre)

14. Malé City Council extension plot ([?] [?] extension)

Whereas those plots are plots already designated to generate income in the council's budget, and the income from those plots is money spent on, for example, [?] the council's administrative running costs, the financial [?] the council receives will be lost when those plots are taken,

[signature]

Whereas making such a decision, at a time when the council is formulating extremely important services and development projects for the people, such as developing parking buildings, recreational parks and open spaces to reduce congestion in Malé, will cause great losses to the council and the [?] people of Malé,

Whereas this decision of the government is a decision that obstructs the system of decentralised administration of the administrative divisions of the Maldives and narrows the legal powers of councils,

Whereas, at the same time, this decision is considered to have been made without completing the legal procedures set out in Article 56-2(d) of Law No. 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act of the Maldives),

As this is a matter that directly [?] the entire decentralised system, we submit this resolution to ascertain the view of members of the 20th People's Majlis on this matter.

Submitting member: South Galolhu constituency MP Meekail Ahmed Nasym
